scheduled_change.what: The city moves to the 2024 International Building Code, 2024 International Plumbing Code and the other 2024 ICC codes, and the 2023 National Electrical Code, with local amendments (Sections 36-600 and following for the building code). The local amendments keep ICC A117.1-2009 as the accessibility standard (in place of the 2017 edition the 2024 code names) and the 2018 energy code. They do not amend Chapter 8, Table 1004.5 or Chapter 29 of the building code, or Chapter 4 of the plumbing code, so from that day the unamended 2024 model text governs toilet counts (same ratios as 2018), the HDPE fire test (803.9, unchanged), single-user room signs (2902.1.2: 'available for use by all persons regardless of their sex') and shared all-gender rooms (2902.2 exception 6, 2902.1.1 exception 2).
scheduled_change.quote: Effective January 1, 2027, the City will transition to the 2024 ICC Codes and the 2023 NEC, including applicable local amendments.
scheduled_change.note: The adopting ordinance (council bill number, date passed) was not found: the amendment PDFs carry no ordinance number and were created 2026-11-20.

fixtures.basis: Springfield enforces the 2018 International Building Code and 2018 International Plumbing Code through 2026-12-31 and the 2024 editions from 2027-01-01. The state pack's worked examples use the 2018 model table (Table 2902.1), and the 2024 table has the same ratios for offices (1 per 25 for the first 50, then 1 per 50), restaurants (1 per 75) and schools (1 per 50), the same split in half and rounding up (2902.1.1) and the same small-occupancy exceptions (2902.2: 15, 100 mercantile, 25 business). Because Springfield adopts the International Plumbing Code, the table's reference to Section 424.2 works: urinals may replace up to 67% of men's toilets in assembly and educational occupancies and 50% elsewhere (2018 and 2024 text). The city's amendments to the 2024 codes, read in full, do not touch any of these. Its amendments to the 2018 codes were not read, so 'no amendment' is confirmed for 2027 onward and unconfirmed for the last weeks of 2026.

quotes.2018_2902.1.1: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
quotes.table: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 / 1 per 75. Business: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50. Educational facilities: 1 per 50 / 1 per 50. (2018 and 2024 Table 2902.1)
quotes.2024_ipc_424.2: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies.
quotes.2018_ipc_424.2: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
quotes.2024_2902.1.1_exc2: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load.

fixtures.hdpe_fire: Applies under both editions: Section 803.9 ('Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1', the NFPA 286 room test) reads the same in the 2018 and 2024 International Building Code, and the city's 2024 amendments do not touch Chapter 8.
fixtures.occupant_load: Table 1004.5, 2018 and 2024 editions alike: business areas 150 gross, assembly unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net, classroom area 20 net. Not amended in the city's 2024 amendments.
fixtures.confidence_note: Model text read on UpCodes (secondary copy; the 2024 text on its Colorado copy, whose state additions are in a separate Section 2904). The city's amendments to the 2024 codes were read on the city's own PDFs; its amendments to the 2018 codes were not read.

The exempt list as it stands today (Section 105.2 of the 2018 code with the city's amendments, in Chapter 36 on Municode) was not read; the unamended 2018 model item 13 reads 'Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height'. page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Springfield, MO job sites. Price your restroom and see the city rules, the 2027 code change and local tax.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Springfield offices, schools, medical centers and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Springfield's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Springfield sets the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** Springfield switches to newer editions of its building and plumbing rules that day. The toilet counts in the table and the fire test for solid plastic stay the same. The rules on restroom signs and shared restrooms change.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Missouri has no state law on single-user or all-gender restrooms, and none on who may use which restroom. Under the building rules Springfield applies until December 31, 2026, a one-person or family restroom is marked for use by either sex, and larger buildings need separate men's and women's rooms. From January 1, 2027 a one-person restroom is signed as open to everyone, and a shared restroom for all users is allowed where every toilet has its own stall with a door and every urinal has a screen.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Springfield requires a building permit to construct, enlarge or alter a building and says some remodeling and repairs are exempt. The exempt list in the rules that start on January 1, 2027 includes painting, tiling, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Building Development Services at 417-864-1585 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Springfield counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and they are the same under the rules that start on January 1, 2027. Separate men's and women's rooms aren't required in a space for 15 people or fewer, in an office for 25 or fewer or in a store for 100 or fewer. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Springfield's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Building Development Services sets the final number.
skip_state_sources: Toilet counts under the model rules
Fire test for solid plastic partitions under the model rules
page.install_rule: Springfield requires a City-licensed general contractor or trade master to be listed on a permit before it is issued. Missouri has no state license for general or specialty interior contractors such as partition installers. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Missouri has no state license for partition installers, and where the work needs a Springfield permit, a City-licensed contractor must be listed on it.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, city, county and school district projects with a total cost above $75,000, Missouri law requires at least the wage the state sets each year for each trade in each county. For a carpenter on building work in Greene County that is $52.16 an hour, benefits included.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.1% at most Springfield addresses: 4.225% state, 1.75% Greene County and 2.125% city. Addresses inside the downtown improvement district pay 8.6%, and other shopping and transportation districts add their own tax. Partitions shipped in from a seller outside Missouri fall under the use tax instead: 6.35% at most addresses and 6.85% in the downtown district.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals, medical offices and college campuses:** phenolic or stainless steel stalls for restrooms that are cleaned many times a day.
